short_description: A bullet-shaped rhabdovirus (family Rhabdoviridae, genus Lyssavirus, species Rabies lyssavirus): roughly 180 nm long by 75 nm across, hemispherically rounded (conical) at one end and flat/slightly concave (planar) at the other. A host-derived lipid envelope, studded over the rounded end and the curved sides with short trimeric glycoprotein (G) spikes but bare over the flat base, encloses an inner matrix (M) protein layer that condenses a helical ribonucleoprotein core - the ~12 kb negative-sense single-stranded RNA genome tightly wound with N (nucleoprotein), plus the L and P proteins - into a tightly coiled, cross-striated skeleton visible in cross-section as ladder-like/herringbone striations.

colour_legend.envelope: soft translucent grey-lilac lipid bilayer, following the bullet outline exactly - hemispherical at one end, flat/slightly concave at the other, never symmetric
colour_legend.glycoprotein_spikes: short, blunt, club-shaped rose/pink studs in a dense honeycomb pattern, covering the rounded end and the full length of the curved sides - explicitly ABSENT from the flat base, which is bare envelope
colour_legend.matrix_protein: thin warm amber/tan lining layer directly under the envelope, hugging the inside of the bullet shape and pinching the coil tight
colour_legend.ribonucleoprotein: coppery-gold tightly wound helical coil filling the interior, showing visible cross-striations (a ladder/herringbone pattern) rather than a smooth solid fill - this is what makes a cutaway read as a real rhabdovirus rather than a cartoon bullet
colour_legend.background: neutral dark charcoal (watercolour: warm aged paper)
colour_legend.note: A virion has no pigment of its own; the real TEM reference (CDC PHIL 1876) is greyscale, so every colour here is teaching convention. Keep this same structure->colour mapping across sem/textbook/3d/watercolor so the set reads as one poster, and keep the same mapping distinct from varicella-zoster-virus's already-used palette (that one is spherical/icosahedral; this one is never spherical).

do_not_draw: a spherical or icosahedral virion - rabies is NEVER round; the bullet silhouette (~2.4:1 long:wide, one end rounded, one end flat) is the whole identity of this plate
a virion rounded at BOTH ends (that is a generic capsule/rod shape, not a rhabdovirus) - exactly one end must be hemispherical and the other must read as flat or slightly concave
glycoprotein spikes on the flat/planar base - ICTV and standard virology sources are explicit that the flat end is bare envelope; spikes belong only on the rounded end and the curved sides
long stalked or rod-like spikes, or spikes drawn as rays/starburst - the real G-protein peplomers are SHORT (5-10 nm) and blunt, in a dense honeycomb, never long projections

a smooth, featureless, solid-fill interior with no internal structure - the coiled ribonucleoprotein must show visible cross-striation/herringbone texture in every cutaway style; a plain smooth core reads as a generic cartoon bullet, not a rhabdovirus

a double-stranded DNA genome, or a genome drawn as loose free RNA outside the ribonucleoprotein coil - the genome is negative-sense single-stranded RNA and it is always shown tightly wound with N protein, never bare
a bacterial cell wall, peptidoglycan, flagellum, pilus, capsule or nucleoid - a virion is not a cell

an icosahedral capsid or a tegument layer (that is the herpesvirus/varicella-zoster-virus plan already used elsewhere in this atlas) - rabies has no icosahedral capsid at all, only the envelope/matrix/RNP three-layer bullet
a dog, bat, fox, or any other animal, and no human figure, in the four science styles (sem/textbook/3d/watercolor) - those are hosts and vectors, not the virus morphology
a distressed, foaming, snarling or aggressive animal anywhere, including the coloring page - this is a frightening disease for a general and child audience and no fear imagery belongs in any style
any baked-in text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars, rulers, legends or watermarks
a black border, dark frame, vignette, letterbox bar, mat, drop shadow, or the artwork drawn as a sheet/card lying on a surface

sources.claim: Rabies virus (Rabies lyssavirus, family Rhabdoviridae, genus Lyssavirus) is bullet-shaped, ~75 x 180 nm (ICTV gives a genus/family range of 100-430 nm long x 45-100 nm diameter for rhabdoviruses generally), with one end hemispherical/conical and the other planar (flat, slightly concave)
sources.source: ICTV 9th Report, Rhabdoviridae chapter (https://ictv.global/report_9th/RNAneg/Mononegavirales/Rhabdoviridae); NCBI Bookshelf, Medical Microbiology 4th ed., ch. 61 'Rhabdoviruses: Rabies Virus' (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK8618/), which gives 75 x 180 nm with 'one end conical, the other planar (concave)'

sources.claim: The outer surface is covered with glycoprotein (G) peplomers/spikes 5-10 nm long and ~3 nm in diameter, trimers of the G protein arranged in a honeycomb pattern, covering the whole surface EXCEPT the quasi-planar (flat) end, which is bare envelope
sources.source: ICTV 9th Report, Rhabdoviridae chapter (https://ictv.global/report_9th/RNAneg/Mononegavirales/Rhabdoviridae); corroborated by NCBI Bookshelf ch. 61, which states the envelope (and its G-protein spikes) does not cover the planar end

sources.claim: Beneath the envelope, the M (matrix) protein (202 aa) lines the inside of the envelope and links it to the ribonucleoprotein, condensing the RNP into a tightly coiled, largely inextensible helical 'skeleton' - this M layer is what gives the coil its cross-striated/herringbone appearance and drives budding even without the G protein
sources.source: Cryo-EM structure paper, 'Cryo-EM structure of the rabies virus ribonucleoprotein complex', Scientific Reports 9:11667 (2019), https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-019-46126-7 and PMC6610074; also PMC254266, 'Dissociation of Rabies Virus Matrix Protein Functions in Regulation of Viral RNA Synthesis and Virus Assembly'

sources.claim: The genome is a single, negative-sense, single-stranded RNA of ~12 kb, tightly and continuously encapsidated by N (nucleoprotein) with the L (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) and P (phosphoprotein) proteins, forming the helical ribonucleoprotein (RNP)/nucleocapsid that occupies the interior and forms a conical tip at the rounded end
sources.source: Scientific Reports 9:11667 (2019) cryo-EM RNP structure paper (as above); NCBI Bookshelf ch. 61 (as above)

sources.claim: Visual confirmation that a real TEM plate (not a diagram) shows numerous elongated, bullet/rod-shaped dark particles with rounded and flatter ends embedded in a granular matrix (a Negri body inclusion)
sources.source: Direct pixel-level inspection of CDC PHIL 1876 hi-res TIFF (crop at ~5-35% width / 20-45% height) - see reference block below

reference.license: Public domain - CDC Public Health Image Library states 'None - This image is in the public domain and thus free of any copyright restrictions.'
reference.modality: thin-section transmission electron microscopy (TEM), greyscale, of infected tissue
reference.native_pixel_size: lores JPEG 700 x 912 px (232,625 bytes, image/jpeg), verified via curl -sIL (HTTP 200, following the phil.cdc.gov -> wwwn.cdc.gov redirect) and Pillow. Hi-res TIFF also confirmed reachable at 1835 x 2392 px, 5,623,116 bytes (image/tiff, HTTP 200) - used for visual verification below; not necessarily the download source (see note).
reference.verified: PHIL caption reads: 'This transmission electron microscopic (TEM) image, reveals some of the ultrastructural features exhibited by numerous bullet-shaped, rabies virus particles, as well as cellular inclusions known as Negri bodies.' Direct pixel-level inspection of the hi-res TIFF confirms this: a dense granular cytoplasmic matrix (a Negri body) contains numerous elongated, oblong dark-grey particles with visibly rounded and flatter ends, consistent with bullet-shaped rabies virions in thin section, though at this magnification the low-power full frame reads as a diffuse granular field - the bullet shape is only clearly legible on a zoomed crop, not in the full lores overview. This is a FIELD of many virions within a Negri body, not a single isolated specimen (the atlas's stated preference), but the caption and a magnified crop both confirm it clearly shows the microbe's diagnostic bullet-shaped particles, satisfying the fallback 'group acceptable if features are clearly readable' rule. Not previously used elsewhere in this atlas (existing PHIL IDs in use: 1878, 10708, 20538, 2172, 8698 - none overlap).
reference.note: fetch_reference.py will center-crop and resize the source to the standard 1080x1080 canvas. Given the low-power full-frame view does not clearly show individual bullet shapes at thumbnail scale, prefer cropping into the denser Negri-body region (roughly the left-third to center of the frame, upper-to-middle band) rather than a naive full-frame center crop, so the labelled reference reads clearly. No baked-in text or scale bar is present on the plate itself, so edit_image.py should be skipped (a plain deterministic crop/resize beats risking re-illustration).
